holidays.name: National Lazy Day
holidays.description: A day dedicated to doing as little as humanly possible. Lounge on the couch, ignore the to-do list, and let guilt-free laziness reign supreme.
holidays.origin: An unofficial observance that circulates widely online and in holiday calendars, with no single known founder. It is celebrated on August 10 in the U.S. as a tongue-in-cheek break from the summer grind.
holidays.funFact: Many sloths sleep or rest for most of the day, which makes them the unofficial mascots of any lazy day.

holidays.name: National S'mores Day
holidays.description: Celebrate the gooey, chocolatey, marshmallowy campfire treat by toasting marshmallows and sandwiching them between graham crackers and chocolate.
holidays.origin: S'mores are a campfire tradition, and the first known published recipe appeared in a 1927 Girl Scouts guidebook under the name 'Some More.' The August 10 food day grew from that tradition.
holidays.funFact: The name 'S'more' is a contraction of 'some more,' which is what people tend to ask for right after finishing their first one.

holidays.name: National Spoil Your Dog Day
holidays.description: A day for pampering your pup with extra treats, belly rubs, new toys, and a very long walk. Dogs everywhere are encouraged to enjoy VIP treatment.
holidays.origin: An unofficial pet-lover observance that has spread through social media and pet-themed holiday calendars, celebrating the bond between people and their dogs.
holidays.funFact: Dogs have been companions to humans for at least 15,000 years, so they have had plenty of time to perfect the art of being spoiled.

holidays.name: Lazy Day Companion: National Garage Sale Day
holidays.description: A day to clear out the clutter, price everything at 50 cents, and haggle with strangers over a lamp from 1987.
holidays.origin: Like many unofficial holidays, it grew out of the American yard-sale culture and is listed by holiday calendars in August, peak garage sale season.
holidays.funFact: The world's longest yard sale, the 127 Yard Sale, stretches roughly 690 miles through several U.S. states every August.
